Image 1 is the PRIMARY and MANDATORY geometric constraint reference.

Image 2 is the PRIMARY reference for ultra-thin control geometry, transparent material expression, and compact consumer-electronics aesthetics.

Image 3 is the original PISCIS rotary-control and product-identity reference.

Image 4 is the functional reference for linear faders and miniature switches.

## PRIMARY TASK — RADICAL LOCAL PANEL RECONSTRUCTION

Redesign ONLY the upper control panel of the PISCIS LAB instrument shown in Image 1.

The existing upper panel is NOT a finished design.

It is only a temporary placeholder indicating the allowable packaging space, original interface components, and external geometric boundaries.

Your task is to COMPLETELY REPLACE the existing upper-panel arrangement with a bold, radically new industrial design concept.

Do not follow the original knob arrangement closely.

Do not merely shrink or rearrange the existing large knobs.

Do not simply place the knob section beside the fader section.

Treat the entire existing control layout as disposable and non-binding.

Explore a completely new interface architecture within the fixed panel boundaries.

## ABSOLUTE GEOMETRIC CONSTRAINTS

Preserve from Image 1:

- Exact overall product dimensions
- Original rectangular footprint
- Enclosure thickness and proportions
- External panel boundaries
- Corner radii
- Mechanical connection between upper and lower sections
- Lower button-grid arrangement
- All lower-panel geometry
- Original orthographic top-down viewing angle
- Original image framing and composition

Do not enlarge the product.

Do not extend the upper panel.

Do not redesign the lower button-grid section.

Do not modify anything outside the masked editing region.

The final product must remain ONE complete, physically unified instrument.

## MANDATORY CONTROL CONFIGURATION

Integrate exactly:

- SIX ultra-low-profile rotary controls
- FIVE compact linear faders
- FOUR miniature mechanical switches

All fifteen controls must fit within ONE continuous upper control panel.

Every control must be visible, individually recognizable, and functionally believable.

The existing panel footprint cannot change.

You may radically modify control placement, diameter, height, orientation, grouping, and visual proportions.

Preserve the functional identity of every control.

The controls must feel physically integrated into one coherent interface, not assembled from separate products.

## IMAGE 2 — TRANSPARENT MATERIAL AND ULTRA-COMPACT DESIGN LANGUAGE

Image 2 is a major industrial design reference.

Extract its distinctive visual and mechanical characteristics:

- Extremely thin product construction
- Low-profile circular controls
- Minimal protrusion above the main surface
- Flush-mounted and partially recessed components
- Tight geometric integration
- Transparent and translucent plastic construction
- Visible internal structural layering
- Precision-molded transparent surfaces
- Subtle internal component visibility
- Lightweight consumer-electronics character
- Refined, understated mechanical detailing

Translate these characteristics into the redesigned PISCIS upper panel.

The rotary knobs should become thin precision rotary discs with shallow vertical profiles.

Use compact diameters, minimal sidewall height, subtle rotational indicators, and closely integrated recessed mounting structures.

Avoid traditional tall synthesizer knobs.

Avoid bulky cylindrical caps and excessive mechanical protrusions.

The controls must remain visibly rotatable rather than resembling ordinary push buttons.

## TRANSPARENT CMF EXPLORATION

Introduce the transparent material language of Image 2 as a KEY VISUAL FEATURE of the redesigned upper panel.

Radically reinterpret the original solid navy-blue panel through transparent and translucent materials.

Explore:

- Translucent blue-tinted polycarbonate
- Smoked transparent blue plastic
- Frosted translucent surface treatments
- Transparent layered panel construction
- Subtle visibility of internal PCB structures
- Precisely integrated transparent mechanical components
- Controlled opacity variations
- Delicate internal structural details
- Refined light transmission and material depth
- Thin transparent surfaces with sophisticated edge treatment

The transparent material must feel intentional, premium, and believable as an injection-molded consumer product.

Create a sophisticated relationship between transparent surfaces, opaque controls, and partially visible internal structures.

Preserve the PISCIS LAB identity through a restrained blue-toned material palette, cream-colored controls, subtle yellow accents, and precise technical details.

The transparent treatment should visually reduce the perceived mass of the upper panel.

It should make the interface feel thinner, lighter, more compact, and more technologically refined.

Avoid excessive transparency that destroys the readability of the control layout.

Avoid chaotic exposed electronics.

Avoid copying the enclosure or arcade-button layout from Image 2.

Use its material and mechanical language as inspiration, not its literal product architecture.

## IMAGE 3 — ORIGINAL PISCIS DESIGN DNA

Image 3 defines the original PISCIS industrial design identity.

Preserve:

- Minimal geometric design language
- Compact modular instrument character
- Restrained visual complexity
- Precise circular control detailing
- Exposed metallic fasteners
- Clean technical typography
- Cream and yellow accent controls
- Premium consumer-electronics sensibility

However, the original six-knob layout is completely non-binding.

The original knob dimensions and thicknesses are also non-binding.

Radically miniaturize and reconstruct these controls using the low-profile mechanical language of Image 2.

## IMAGE 4 — FADER AND SWITCH FUNCTIONAL REFERENCE

Image 4 defines the functional characteristics of the linear faders and miniature switches.

Integrate five miniature linear faders and four compact switches into the redesigned PISCIS upper panel.

Explore:

- Short-travel linear controls
- Slim recessed fader channels
- Low-profile slider handles
- Compact mechanical switches
- Integrated slot geometry
- Highly compressed component spacing
- Refined tactile surfaces
- Precise control labeling

Do not copy the original red-panel arrangement.

Do not reproduce its enclosure.

Use the components as a functional vocabulary for a completely new interface composition.

## RADICAL INDUSTRIAL DESIGN EXPLORATION

Prioritize:

- Aggressive spatial compression
- Extreme interface miniaturization
- Bold and unconventional control grouping
- Architectural organization
- Strong visual hierarchy
- Precise geometric rhythm
- Sophisticated asymmetry
- Interwoven circular and linear controls
- Unexpected but ergonomic arrangements
- Highly refined negative space
- Thin layered surface geometry
- Recessed control integration
- Subtle mechanical depth
- Strong material contrast
- Advanced transparent CMF treatment
- Minimal visual clutter
- Exceptionally precise component detailing

The redesigned upper panel should feel significantly different from both original PISCIS control panels.

Explore daring and experimental interface compositions.

Do not merely produce a cleaner version of the existing design.

The result should demonstrate genuine industrial design innovation through new component relationships, compact packaging, translucent material expression, and sophisticated geometric organization.

Push the design as far as possible within the fixed panel boundaries.

Maintain plausible manufacturing logic, realistic control clearance, and believable finger accessibility.

## FINAL DESIGN CHARACTER

The result should feel like an exceptionally refined, compact, transparent electronic musical instrument.

Combine the playful precision of experimental consumer electronics with the visual discipline of professional musical equipment.

Emphasize:

- Ultra-thin mechanical controls
- Transparent blue polycarbonate
- Cream-colored precision rotary discs
- Compact recessed faders
- Minimal switches
- Subtle yellow accents
- Delicate visible internal structure
- Tight, sophisticated component packaging
- Premium industrial design detailing

The final product should feel lighter, thinner, more compact, and more advanced than the original.

## FINAL OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS

Generate exactly ONE complete physical PISCIS LAB instrument.

Redesign ONLY the masked upper control panel.

All six rotary controls, five linear faders, and four switches must coexist on that single panel.

Preserve the entire lower button-grid section unchanged.

Preserve the original enclosure footprint, camera orientation, external boundaries, and image framing.

STRICT ORTHOGRAPHIC TOP-DOWN VIEW.

No perspective transformation.

No second instrument.

No additional modules.

No separated control panels.

No oversized knobs.

No conventional bulky synthesizer controls.

No changes outside the masked region.

The final image should look like an advanced, production-believable industrial design concept featuring radically redesigned control architecture, exceptionally compact mechanical integration, and sophisticated translucent material expression.

Image 5 and Image 6 are additional aesthetic/material/detail references ONLY. Extract visual language, manufacturable surface detailing, and finish. Never copy their outer enclosure, camera view, proportions, or control counts. Image 1 overrides all other visual references.

White studio background, exact top-down orthographic single-product concept render.

# FLUX.2 Klein — 3-prompt comparison / 6 image references

- Input 1 = locked geometry, 2–6 = style / components / materials. **Replace image 5 and image 6 before running**.
- Edit the large `PROMPT A`, `PROMPT B`, `PROMPT C` text boxes independently. Same 6 reference images + same initial fixed seed for controlled comparisons.
- One shared mask defines **WHITE = upper panel to redraw** and **BLACK = preserve**; align it with reference image 1.
- Sampling geometry **384 × 480**; final PNG saved via `OUTPUT A/B/C` at **320 × 400** to reduce disk usage and preview size.
- The external VAEEncode -> SetLatentNoiseMask supplies all three branches, avoids the original cycle, then ImageCompositeMasked restores unmasked pixels directly from Image 1.
- When changing output resolution, keep the 6 reference ImageScale nodes, mask ImageScale, and final output scale nodes consistent.
- Prompt A retains your full previous detailed wording. B and C introduce compact, differentiated design directions.
